problems.reason: All three sentences state that Spiclypeus is classified within the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
Both sentences assert that Spiclypeus is a sister species to a clade containing Kosmoceratops and Vagaceratops, rather than being closely related to Triceratops.
Both sentences provide the age of Spiclypeus, stating it lived around 76 million years ago.
Both sentences state that perforations in the frill were caused by intraspecific combat with an opponent’s brow horns.
Both sentences present the same phylogenetic relationship, describing Spiclypeus as a sister species to a clade containing Kosmoceratops and Vagaceratops.
Sentence 9 refers to “the bone” and “the joint” without specifying which bone or joint was previously mentioned, leaving the reference unclear.
Sentences 11‑13 discuss the land purchase, excavation team, and hiring of an amateur paleontologist—details about the site and personnel rather than the animal itself.
